title: Schema‑gated tool-call flow: resumable streams, deprecation handling, and runtime error classes — acceptance criteria
creator: Aisha Moreno
summary: Define acceptance criteria for a backwards-compatible, schema-gated tool/function calling flow that supports resumable streamed emissions, explicit error classes, and deprecation/migration signals. This PRD focuses on runtime behavior, observable signals, and e2e verification so client SDKs and server runtimes can implement interoperable handshakes and graceful fallbacks.
background: Teams have implemented multiple streaming structured-output contracts and tool-calling variants. We need a single, pragmatic acceptance spec that: 1) makes tool-calls schema-aware (schema-gated), 2) supports partial/streamed emission checkpoints and resume tokens, 3) defines error taxonomies so clients can distinguish recoverable vs non-recoverable conditions, and 4) includes deprecation/version signals so older clients degrade gracefully.
goals: Specify schema-gated tool invocation handshake (version + optional schema URL) and runtime validation points.
Define resumable streaming checkpoints with single-word resume tokens and checkpoint envelopes.
Standardize error classes: recoverable, non-recoverable, transient, schema-mismatch, and tool-deprecated.
Lay out e2e test cases and telemetry assertions required for release.
Provide migration guidelines for SDKs and customers to adopt the new handshake with minimal disruption.
non_goals: Mandating a particular wire-format for tool payloads beyond JSON envelopes (we accept both application/json and newline-delimited typed frames).
Implementing language-specific SDKs (this is a platform-level acceptance spec).
Changing authentication or billing behavior for tool calls.
acceptance_criteria: Handshake: The server must accept a tool call request that includes: tool_id (string), tool_version (semver string or "latest"), schema_id (optional string), and optional schema_url (http(s) URL). If schema_url is present server will attempt validation against that schema and emit validation results in telemetry and response envelopes.

Checkpoint envelopes: Streamed responses that include structured objects must periodically emit a checkpoint envelope: {"type":"checkpoint", "resume_token":"<opaque-token>", "progress": <0-100>}. Clients must be able to resume from any checkpoint token; resumption should not require replaying tokens older than the latest acknowledged checkpoint.

Resume semantics: A resumed request that supplies a valid resume_token will produce the remainder of the response (idempotent) and must not duplicate already committed objects beyond a deterministic reordering tolerance window. Server must return explicit 'resume_ack' envelope on resume indicating starting offset and any trim information.

Error taxonomy in-band: Responses must classify errors using a stable string field error_class with allowed values ["recoverable", "transient", "non_recoverable", "schema_mismatch", "tool_deprecated"]. Clients and SDKs should treat schema_mismatch and tool_deprecated as actionable signals for migration UI/telemetry.

Graceful fallback: If server detects schema_mismatch and client supplied schema_url, server must emit a 'partial_emit' envelope with the objects that validated, plus a 'validation_report' envelope listing failing elements. If no validated objects exist, server should return a single canonical error envelope and a documented HTTP status (422 for validation failure when request body included schema_url).

Backpressure and pause: For long-running tool calls, server must emit periodic heartbeat envelopes and respect a client 'pause' frame. When client sends a pause-with-ack frame, server should pause new emission for up to configured PauseTimeout (default 30s) and resume when client sends a resume frame or timeout expires. Pause semantics must be exposed in docs and visible in telemetry.

Deprecation handshake: When a tool version is marked deprecated, server must include 'tool_deprecated' reason and suggested replacement tool_id/version in a 'deprecation_notice' envelope. New calls to deprecated versions should be allowed for a configurable grace period but must log tenant-visible warnings and increment a deprecation telemetry counter.

Idempotency and dedup: Tool calls that mutate downstream systems must accept an idempotency_key field. Server must guarantee at-least-once deliverability for streaming flows but de-duplicate side-effects when idempotency_key is present. Idempotency guarantees must be documented.

Observability: Server must record telemetry for each tool call: schema_validation_rate, checkpoint_frequency, average_resume_latency, error_class_counts, bytes_streamed, and deprecation_warnings. Dashboards for these metrics must be available in Console-per-route within the release window.

E2E tests: Automated tests covering 1) resume after partial emit, 2) schema mismatch with partial emit + validation report, 3) pause/resume under backpressure, 4) deprecation notice emitted + telemetry increment, 5) idempotency dedupe for at-least-once delivery must exist and pass in CI.
test_cases: Resume token replay: Start a tool call that emits 3 objects and a checkpoint; close connection abruptly; reopen with resume_token -> verify object stream continues and no duplicates beyond tolerance window.
Schema mismatch partial: Call tool with schema_url that deliberately rejects last field -> expect partial_emit and validation_report with failing path, HTTP 422 if no valid objects.
Pause/resume behavior: Client sends pause frame during high-volume streaming, server pauses, then resume frame -> ensure pause honored and heartbeat envelopes emitted during pause window.
Deprecation flow: Call a deprecated tool_version -> verify deprecation_notice envelope, deprecation telemetry increment, and suggested replacement present.
Idempotency dedupe: Send duplicate requests with same idempotency_key causing downstream side-effect -> verify single side-effect executed and subsequent attempts return idempotent success code.
qa_checklist: All acceptance criteria have at least one automated test in CI.
Runtime emits documented envelope types and shapes; sample payloads added to docs.
Console dashboard surfaces the required telemetry by route/tool.
SDKs include helper for resume_token handling and pause/resume frames in the next release; compatibility tests included.
Security reviewed: no additional data exfiltration risk from resume tokens or schema URLs.
rollout_plan: Roll out in three phases: 1) opt-in beta for selected tenants with feature flag (2 weeks), 2) broader internal canary for all dev/test tenants (1 week), 3) gradual public rollout with deprecation warnings for replaced tools (2-4 weeks). Monitor telemetry and have rollback toggle ready.
telemetry_metrics: schema_validation_rate: percent of requests with schema_url that pass validation
average_resume_latency_ms: wall time between resume request and first resumed token
error_class_counts: counts by error_class per route
deprecation_warnings: occurrences per tenant per day
dependencies: ENG-21042 (runtime: envelope framing and resume_token storage)
ENG-21458 (console: telemetry ingestion and per-route dashboards)
ENG-21999 (sdk: resume and pause helpers in JS/Python SDKs)
PM-100120 (policy: deprecation notice lifecycle and comms)
risks: Resume token replay increases state retention on serving node clusters; must bound retention window to avoid memory blowup.
Schema validation at runtime can add CPU cost; may require sampling or offloading validation to a worker pool.
Clients that do not adopt resume semantics will see degraded UX during interruptions; migration communications needed.
Deprecation grace periods might prolong technical debt if not enforced.
